paper_info.title: Attention Is All You Need
paper_info.abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature.

presentation_flow.background_context: Sequence transduction models have been dominated by recurrent neural networks (RNNs), long short-term memory (LSTM), and gated recurrent neural networks (GRU) for tasks like language modeling and machine translation. These models factor computation along symbol positions of input and output sequences, generating hidden states as a function of previous hidden states and current input. Attention mechanisms have become integral to sequence modeling, allowing dependency modeling without regard to distance in sequences. However, attention mechanisms have traditionally been used in conjunction with recurrent networks. The field has seen numerous efforts to push boundaries of recurrent language models and encoder-decoder architectures, with works like Extended Neural GPU, ByteNet, and ConvS2S attempting to reduce sequential computation using convolutional neural networks as basic building blocks.
presentation_flow.problem_motivation: Recurrent models have an inherently sequential nature that precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longer sequence lengths as memory constraints limit batching across examples. The fundamental constraint of sequential computation remains despite improvements through factorization tricks and conditional computation. In convolutional approaches like ConvS2S and ByteNet, the number of operations required to relate signals from two arbitrary positions grows with distance between positions (linearly for ConvS2S, logarithmically for ByteNet), making it difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions. Existing state-of-the-art models require significant training time and computational resources, with ensemble methods needed to achieve best results. The sequential nature of RNNs creates O(n) sequential operations where n is sequence length, limiting training efficiency.
presentation_flow.solution_overview: The Transformer is a new model architecture that eschews recurrence entirely and relies solely on attention mechanisms to draw global dependencies between input and output. It follows an encoder-decoder structure using stacked self-attention and point-wise fully connected layers for both encoder and decoder. The encoder is composed of N=6 identical layers, each with two sub-layers: multi-head self-attention mechanism and position-wise fully connected feed-forward network. The decoder also has N=6 identical layers but inserts a third sub-layer performing multi-head attention over encoder output. The model employs residual connections around each sub-layer followed by layer normalization. All sub-layers produce outputs of dimension d_model=512. The Transformer allows significantly more parallelization and can reach new state-of-the-art in translation quality after training for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.
presentation_flow.technical_approach: The core attention function maps queries and key-value pairs to output vectors, computed as weighted sum of values where weights come from query-key compatibility. Scaled Dot-Product Attention computes: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T/√d_k)V, where scaling by √d_k counteracts large dot product magnitudes that push softmax into small gradient regions. Multi-Head Attention linearly projects queries, keys, and values h times with different learned projections to d_k, d_k, and d_v dimensions, performing attention in parallel on each projected version. The model uses h=8 parallel attention heads with d_k=d_v=d_model/h=64. Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks apply two linear transformations with ReLU activation: FFN(x) = max(0, xW_1+b_1)W_2+b_2, with d_model=512 and d_ff=2048. Positional Encoding uses sine and cosine functions of different frequencies to inject sequence order information since the model contains no recurrence or convolution. Training uses Adam optimizer with learning rate schedule: lrate = d_model^(-0.5) · min(step_num^(-0.5), step_num · warmup_steps^(-1.5)) with warmup_steps=4000.
presentation_flow.evidence_proof: On WMT 2014 English-to-German translation, Transformer (big) achieves 28.4 BLEU, outperforming best previously reported models including ensembles by over 2.0 BLEU, with training taking 3.5 days on 8 P100 GPUs. The base model achieves 27.3 BLEU at fraction of training cost (3.3·10^18 FLOPs vs 7.7·10^19 for ConvS2S Ensemble). On WMT 2014 English-to-French, big model achieves 41.8 BLEU (new single-model state-of-the-art) at less than 1/4 training cost of previous state-of-the-art. Table 1 shows Self-Attention has O(1) sequential operations vs O(n) for Recurrent and O(log_k(n)) for Convolutional, with O(1) maximum path length vs O(n) for Recurrent. Model variations show single-head attention is 0.9 BLEU worse than best 8-head setting, and reducing attention key size hurts quality. Transformer generalizes to English constituency parsing, achieving 91.3 F1 on WSJ only (vs 91.7 best previous) and 92.7 F1 semi-supervised (vs 92.1 best previous), outperforming RNN sequence-to-sequence models even with only 40K training sentences.
presentation_flow.impact_significance: The Transformer represents the first sequence transduction model based entirely on attention, replacing recurrent layers most commonly used in encoder-decoder architectures with multi-headed self-attention. For translation tasks, it can be trained significantly faster than architectures based on recurrent or convolutional layers while achieving new state-of-the-art on both WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French tasks. The best model outperforms all previously reported ensembles on English-to-German. Self-attention yields more interpretable models where individual attention heads learn to perform different tasks related to syntactic and semantic structure. Future work includes applying attention-based models to other tasks, extending Transformer to problems with input/output modalities other than text (images, audio, video), investigating local restricted attention mechanisms for large inputs/outputs, and making generation less sequential. Code is available at github.com/tensorflow/tensor2tensor.

equations.analysis: This is the core Scaled Dot-Product Attention formula that computes attention weights. The scaling factor √d_k prevents dot products from growing too large in magnitude, which would push softmax into regions with extremely small gradients. This formula enables parallel computation of attention across all query positions simultaneously, unlike sequential RNN approaches.

In this work, h=8 parallel attention heads are used.

equations.context: In addition to attention sub-layers, each of the layers in our encoder and decoder contains a fully connected feed-forward network, which is applied to each position separately and identically. This consists of two linear transformations with a ReLU activation in between. The dimensionality of input and output is dmodel = 512, and the inner-layer has dimensionality df f = 2048.
equations.analysis: This defines the Position-wise Feed-Forward Network applied to each position separately and identically in encoder and decoder layers. It consists of two linear transformations with ReLU activation between them. While linear transformations are same across positions, they use different parameters from layer to layer. This can also be described as two convolutions with kernel size 1.

equations.context: In this work, we use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies: where pos is the position and i is the dimension. That is, each dimension of the positional encoding corresponds to a sinusoid. The wavelengths form a geometric progression from 2π to 10000 · 2π. We chose this function because we hypothesized it would allow the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions.
equations.analysis: This formula defines the sinusoidal Positional Encoding added to input embeddings to inject sequence order information since the model contains no recurrence or convolution. Each dimension corresponds to a sinusoid with wavelengths forming geometric progression. This allows the model to learn to attend by relative positions since for any fixed offset k, PE_pos+k can be represented as linear function of PE_pos.

equations.context: We used the Adam optimizer with β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.98 and ϵ = 10−9. We varied the learning rate over the course of training, according to the formula. This corresponds to increasing the learning rate linearly for the first warmup_steps training steps, and decreasing it thereafter proportionally to the inverse square root of the step number. equations.analysis: This learning rate schedule formula increases learning rate linearly for first 4000 warmup steps, then decreases proportionally to inverse square root of step number. This adaptive schedule helps stabilize training in early steps while allowing convergence in later stages. Combined with Adam optimizer, this enables efficient training of the Transformer architecture.

tables.analysis: This table demonstrates the computational advantages of Self-Attention over Recurrent and Convolutional layers. Self-Attention requires only O(1) sequential operations compared to O(n) for Recurrent, enabling full parallelization. Maximum path length is O(1) for Self-Attention vs O(n) for Recurrent, making it easier to learn long-range dependencies. This quantifies why Transformer can train significantly faster than RNN-based models while better capturing distant relationships in sequences.

tables.caption: Table 2: The Transformer achieves better BLEU scores than previous state-of-the-art models on the English-to-German and English-to-French newstest2014 tests at a fraction of the training cost
tables.analysis: This table shows Transformer's superior performance with dramatically lower training costs. Transformer (big) achieves 28.4 BLEU on EN-DE (vs 26.36 best ensemble) and 41.8 BLEU on EN-FR (vs 41.29 best ensemble). Training cost is 2.3·10^19 FLOPs vs 7.7·10^19 for ConvS2S Ensemble on EN-DE, representing significant efficiency gains. Even the base model at 3.3·10^18 FLOPs outperforms all previous single models. This demonstrates Transformer achieves state-of-the-art quality at fraction of computational cost.

tables.caption: Table 3: Variations on the Transformer architecture
tables.analysis: This ablation study reveals critical architecture design choices. Single-head attention (h=1) performs 0.9 BLEU worse than 8-head base, showing multi-head is essential. Reducing attention key size d_k hurts quality (25.1 vs 25.8 BLEU), suggesting compatibility determination is not easy. Bigger models perform better (d_model=1024 achieves 26.0 BLEU vs 24.5 for d_model=256). Dropout is very helpful (0.1 rate optimal, 0.0 drops to 24.6 BLEU). Sinusoidal vs learned positional embeddings produce nearly identical results (25.8 vs 25.7 BLEU). Big model with 213M params achieves 26.4 BLEU on dev set.

tables.analysis: This table demonstrates Transformer's generalization beyond machine translation to English constituency parsing. With WSJ only training (40K sentences), Transformer achieves 91.3 F1, outperforming most previous models and approaching best (91.7). In semi-supervised setting (17M sentences), Transformer achieves 92.7 F1, surpassing all previous semi-supervised models (best previous 92.1). This shows Transformer outperforms RNN sequence-to-sequence models even in small-data regimes where RNNs have struggled, proving the architecture generalizes well to tasks with strong structural constraints.

figures.caption: The Transformer - model architecture showing encoder-decoder structure with stacked self-attention and feed-forward layers
figures.analysis: This figure shows the complete Transformer architecture with encoder stack (left) and decoder stack (right). Encoder has 6 identical layers, each with multi-head self-attention and position-wise feed-forward network with residual connections and layer normalization. Decoder also has 6 layers but adds encoder-decoder attention sub-layer between self-attention and feed-forward. Masking in decoder self-attention prevents positions from attending to subsequent positions. All sub-layers produce d_model=512 dimensional outputs. Input/output embeddings are multiplied by √d_model. This visual is essential for understanding the overall model structure.

figures.caption: Scaled Dot-Product Attention (left) and Multi-Head Attention with parallel attention layers (right)
figures.analysis: Left side shows Scaled Dot-Product Attention mechanism where queries, keys, and values produce attention weights through softmax(QK^T/√d_k)V. Right side shows Multi-Head Attention with h parallel attention heads, each with different learned linear projections. Queries, keys, and values are projected h times to d_k, d_k, d_v dimensions, attention computed in parallel, then concatenated and projected to final output. This enables attending to information from different representation subspaces at different positions simultaneously.

figures.caption: Attention mechanism following long-distance dependencies in encoder self-attention layer 5, showing verb 'making' attending to complete phrase 'making...more difficult'
figures.analysis: This visualization shows encoder self-attention in layer 5 of 6 following long-distance dependencies. Many attention heads attend to distant dependency of verb 'making', completing the phrase 'making...more difficult'. Different colors represent different attention heads. This demonstrates that individual attention heads clearly learn to perform different tasks and exhibit behavior related to syntactic and semantic structure of sentences. The attention is sharp and focused on relevant distant words, showing the model successfully captures long-range dependencies.

figures.caption: Two attention heads in layer 5 involved in anaphora resolution, showing sharp attention from word 'its' to antecedents
figures.analysis: This figure shows two attention heads in layer 5 of 6 apparently involved in anaphora resolution. Top shows full attentions for head 5. Bottom shows isolated attentions from just the word 'its' for attention heads 5 and 6. The attentions are very sharp for this word, clearly connecting 'its' to its antecedent. This demonstrates that different attention heads learn specialized functions - some handle syntactic relationships, others handle semantic coreference. The sharp attention patterns show the model learns interpretable linguistic structures.

figures.caption: Attention heads exhibiting behavior related to sentence structure, showing different heads performing different tasks in encoder self-attention layer 5
figures.analysis: This visualization shows two examples from different attention heads in encoder self-attention at layer 5 of 6. Many attention heads exhibit behavior that seems related to the structure of the sentence. The heads clearly learned to perform different tasks - some focus on syntactic dependencies, others on semantic relationships. This interpretability is a side benefit of self-attention, making the model more transparent than black-box RNN approaches. The attention distributions reveal the model learns meaningful linguistic patterns without explicit supervision.
